name: anon-rpc example
description: Minimal MV3 extension that answers RPC through a hash-pinned anon-rpc worker.
//permissions: offscreen is what lets the extension have a DOM at all. A service worker cannot hold the sandboxed iframe that §6 isolation is built from.
//host_permissions: For the OFFSCREEN document's fetch of the worker bundle, which is hash-verified (§4). The worker's own fetches do NOT use these — it runs at a null origin, so its requests are ordinary cross-origin ones subject to CORS. The e2e proves both halves: it serves the bundle from an endpoint with no CORS headers (the offscreen document gets it) and then has the worker try one (it cannot).
//sandbox: Serves this page at an opaque origin with its own CSP. It is what isolates worker code from the extension, AND what makes running a remotely-fetched bundle permissible at all: Chrome's ban on remotely hosted code carves out sandboxed iframes explicitly.

content_security_policy.//sandbox: Every token is load-bearing. allow-scripts: the boot script. blob: in script-src: the worker runtime AND the worker bundle are both importScripts'd from blob URLs, and importScripts is checked against script-src — omit it and the bundle fails to load with a bare 'failed to load'. blob: in child-src/worker-src: the Web Worker itself is spawned from one. connect-src *: reaching an RPC endpoint is the worker's entire job.
content_security_policy.sandbox: sandbox allow-scripts; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval' blob:; child-src 'self' blob:; worker-src 'self' blob:; connect-src *;

//web_accessible_resources: Deliberately absent. The sandboxed page is framed by an extension page rather than by a web page, so it needs no declaration — established by removing it and watching the e2e still pass.
